title: "21 - Data Processing"
output: html_document

## Purpose

This file loads the clean data, adds new variables, compares deaths during
the pandemic with 2019, and saves the result as `22_DataSaving.RData`.

## 1. Load our functions and the clean data

We load our processing functions and the clean data from the last file.

```{r load}
source("02_funct_DataProcessing.R")
load("12_DataSaving.RData")
dim(df_clean)
```

The clean data has 3,600 rows and 20 columns, as expected.

## 2. Add new variables

We add five new variables:

- `unnatural`: deaths not from natural causes (like injuries), which is all
  deaths minus natural deaths
- `neuro_total`: Alzheimer's disease plus stroke deaths
- `other_natural`: natural deaths not in any of the listed causes
- `period`: "Pre-pandemic" (before March 2020) or "Pandemic"
- `time_index`: the month number, from 1 (January 2019) to 30 (June 2021)

```{r derive}
df_proc <- add_derived_variables(df_clean)
table(df_proc$period)
summary(df_proc$other_natural)
```

There are 1,680 pre-pandemic rows (14 months) and 1,920 pandemic rows (16
months). The smallest value of `other_natural` is 0, so it is never negative,
which is what we expect.

## 3. Change in deaths from 2019 to 2020

The data does not include population sizes, so we cannot find death rates.
Instead, we compare the number of deaths in 2020 with 2019. We leave out
COVID-19 here because it had no deaths in 2019.

```{r overall}
causes_compared <- c("all_cause", "unnatural", "neuro_total",
                     cause_cols[cause_cols != "covid_underlying"])
overall <- percent_change_table(df_proc, causes_compared)
sort(overall[1, ], decreasing = TRUE)
```

Total deaths went up 18.8% in 2020. Among the causes, diabetes (16.7%),
unnatural deaths (13.6%) and Alzheimer's disease (10.5%) went up the most. Chronic lower respiratory
disease is the only cause that went down (-2.7%).

## 4. Change by race/ethnicity

We compare each race/ethnicity group with its own deaths in 2019. This way,
the size of each group does not matter.

```{r by_race}
percent_change(df_proc, "all_cause", group_var = "race_ethnicity")
percent_change_table(df_proc, c("all_cause", "alzheimer", "stroke"),
                     group_var = "race_ethnicity")
```

Deaths went up 44.8% for Hispanic people but 13.9% for White people. Every
other group went up between 26% and 37%. Alzheimer's and stroke deaths show
the same pattern: White people had the smallest increase.

## 5. Change by age group

We compare total deaths and unnatural deaths for each age group.

```{r by_age}
percent_change_table(df_proc, c("all_cause", "unnatural"),
                     group_var = "age_group")
```

For ages 15 to 44, total deaths went up about 21% to 27%, and unnatural
deaths went up about 23%. For ages 75 and over, unnatural deaths went
up less than 3%. So younger adults had a large increase in deaths that were
not natural.

## 6. Change in 2021

Our 2021 data only covers January to June, so we compare it with January to
June of 2019.

```{r year_2021}
percent_change(df_proc, "all_cause", group_var = "race_ethnicity",
               year = 2021, max_month = 6)
```

The gap grew in early 2021. Deaths went up 50.7% for Hispanic people but
10.4% for White people.

## 7. Save the processed data

We save the processed data so the visualization file can use it.

```{r save}
save(df_proc, cause_cols, file = "22_DataSaving.RData")
dim(df_proc)
```

The processed data has 3,600 rows and 25 columns. It is saved as
`22_DataSaving.RData`.
